findings.claim: The learning/control support is the score-clock window [0.0, 0.49] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing; the objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only.

For landmark_00_local_dx the observed endpoint-world coordinate contrast is non-monotone across the window: it rises to a positive peak near t~0.11, falls to a negative trough near t~0.19, partially recovers, and ends near zero; the whole-window mean z is small (-0.18) while first and last node rates have opposite signs (first_rate_z -17.5, last_rate_z +8.1).

The landmark_00_local_dx trend is not well described by a low-order polynomial (polynomial_accepted false, relative_node_RMSE 0.78) and shows 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches, so a single global monotone direction is not supported for this coordinate.

hypotheses.direction: test a smooth staged blend of early same-clock historical forecasts toward frozen static teachers (S1) versus the constant-blend control (S2) at fixed dose
hypotheses.falsifier: if the S1 staged blend produces no reproducible difference from the S2 constant-blend control in the landmark_00_local_dx contrast profile, or if the sign-change pattern is not reproducible across independent batches, the stage-dependent relevance hypothesis is not supported
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx endpoint-world coordinate contrast z over the observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_dx endpoint coordinate contrast changes sign within the observed window, so a stage-dependent (time-varying) teacher relevance or geometric response scale may merit testing at fixed dose rather than a single static endpoint target.

hypotheses.direction: retain a smooth gradual blend rather than introducing a sharp phase knot
hypotheses.falsifier: a reproducible, independently stable profile that localizes a single transition knot would justify a data-derived knot instead of a gradual blend
hypotheses.observable: sign_changes and strong_sign_conflicts of the landmark_00_local_dx contrast, plus per-node reproducibility across independent batches
hypotheses.statement: Because the landmark_00_local_dx contrast is non-monotone with multiple sign changes and no accepted polynomial, any staged schedule should remain gradual with no data-derived knot unless an independently stable profile supports one.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curves were read, so no stage-boundary evidence is claimed.
Only one coordinate feature (landmark_00_local_dx) was read in detail; other landmark coordinates were not inspected and may behave differently.
The contrast curve is a coordinate observable, not an absolute affinity target or spatial gradient; no absolute target is inferred from it.
Selection/survival and decoded final affinity labels are not available in this role input, so no claim about descendant survival or measured final benefit is made.
The observed sign changes are a diagnostic of time-varying contrast, not permission to reverse the affinity objective.
